example.title: Kelleyville Bridge (Bridge No. 085/101), NH Routes 11/103 over the Sugar River

brief: Two-lane state-highway concrete bridge of 1933, 314.5 ft long: a 120 ft open-spandrel twin-rib arch over the river plus five reinforced-concrete T-beam deck spans of 31.6-35 ft on multi-column bents with haunched cap beams and flared column heads; 10-inch deck with deep cross beams, no sidewalks. The original concrete open-balustrade railings were replaced by aluminium horizontal rails. For the 6.2 m highway crossing use one T-beam approach span of this design with the same bent and railing detail.

traits.railing_detail: original open concrete balustrade (later aluminium rails)
